generated.what_happened: Paramount Skydance reached a settlement with California Attorney General Rob Bonta, 11 other state attorneys general, and the Writers Guild of America to resolve an antitrust lawsuit challenging its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Under the terms of the agreement, the merged entity committed to increasing U.S. film production spending, guaranteeing 30 to 32 theatrical releases annually, establishing independent editorial boards for CBS News and CNN, and funding workforce development. Although state officials emphasized that the settlement does not represent an endorsement of further media consolidation, it imposes strict compliance penalties and enables the acquisition to move forward toward closing. This resolution allows Paramount to avoid an extended court trial and substantial delay fees while combining two major film studios, streaming services, and television networks.
